fixes.explanation: Harvest is a good guess, friend, but it's not in this line. The songwriter says to proclaim His loving devotion in the morning and His faithfulness at night (Psalm 92:2). Harvest is a season, and morning and night show up every single day. My oven timer and I have met both of them plenty.

Glory in the temple sounds lovely, friend, and I almost picked it myself. But the songwriter says, “My eyes see the downfall of my enemies…” (Psalm 92:11) There's no temple in this line. After all that harp music, that's a plot twist.

Other way around, friend. The songwriter says, “In old age they will still bear fruit; healthy and green they will remain…” (Psalm 92:14) So old age doesn't stop the fruit. The verse says they keep bearing it. That's good news for anybody with a few birthdays behind them, and I'm cheering.

Yes, friend. The verse says they remain that way to proclaim, “The LORD is upright; He is my Rock, and in Him there is no unrighteousness.” (Psalm 92:15) So the song ends with the proclaiming, which is where it started. It opened with praise and it closes with praise.

Feeding the poor is a good thing, friend. It's not what this verse says, though. Here they stay healthy and green to proclaim, “The LORD is upright; He is my Rock, and in Him there is no unrighteousness.” (Psalm 92:15) What they proclaim is the point.
